'''Stephen Shing-Toung Yau''' ({{lang-zh|t=丘成棟|p=Qiū Chéngdòng}}; born 1952) is a Chinese-American mathematician. He is a Distinguished Professor Emeritus at the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]], and currently teaches at [[Tsinghua University]]. He is a Fellow of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] and the [[American Mathematical Society]].

== Biography ==
Shing-Toung Yau was born in 1952 in [[British Hong Kong]],<ref name="hrbeu">{{Cite news |title=学术报告 |url=http://kjc.hrbeu.edu.cn/2012/0810/c3499a123627/page.htm|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190817005710/http://kjc.hrbeu.edu.cn/2012/0810/c3499a123627/page.htm|date=2012-08-10|archive-date=17 August 2019|access-date=2019-08-17|website=Harbin Engineering University|language=zh}}</ref> with his [[Ancestral home (Chinese)|ancestral home]] in [[Jiaoling County]], [[Guangdong]], China. He is the younger brother of [[Fields Medal]]ist [[Shing-Tung Yau]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2018-06-06|title=丘成桐院士关注家乡蕉岭仓海诗廊文化建设项目|url=http://mini.eastday.com/a/180606031309193.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190817005009/http://mini.eastday.com/a/180606031309193.html|archive-date=17 August 2019|access-date=2019-08-17|website=Eastday|language=zh}}</ref>

After graduating from the [[Chinese University of Hong Kong]], he studied mathematics at the [[State University of New York at Stony Brook]], where he learnt after [[Henry Laufer]]<ref name="hrbeu" /> and earned his M.A. in 1974 and Ph.D. in 1976.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2019-07-11|title=Stephen Shing-Toung Yau|url=https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~yau/yauvitae.pdf|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-08-16|website=University of Illinois at Chicago|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Stephen S. -T Yau|url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37287943600|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-08-17|website=IEEE Xplore|language=en}}</ref>

He was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] at [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton]] from 1976 to 1977 and from 1981 to 1982, and was a Benjamin Pierce Assistant Professor at [[Harvard University]] from 1977 to 1980. He subsequently taught at the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]] for more than 30 years. He was named the UIC Distinguished Professor in 2005.<ref name=":1" />

From 2002 to 2011, Yau also served as the Zi-Jiang Professor at [[East China Normal University]] in [[Shanghai]], as well as Director of the university's Institute of Mathematics.<ref name=":0" /> After retiring from UIC in 2012, he joined [[Tsinghua University]] as a full-time professor.<ref name=":1" />

==Research==
Among Yau's research interests are [[bioinformatics]], [[complex algebraic geometry]], singularities theory, and nonlinear filtering.<ref name=":1" /> He published nearly 300 papers and established the "Yau algebra" and the "Yau number".<ref>{{Cite web|last=瑛|first=杨|date=2012-08-13|title=复几何、奇点理论及相关领域国际会议在清华举行|url=https://www.tsinghua.edu.cn/publish/thunews/10303/2012/20120813152615411357568/20120813152615411357568_.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190817011745/https://www.tsinghua.edu.cn/publish/thunews/10303/2012/20120813152615411357568/20120813152615411357568_.html|archive-date=17 August 2019|access-date=2019-08-17|website=Tsinghua University|language=zh}}</ref> He served as Chairman of the IEEE International Conference on Control and Information and co-founded the ''Journal of Algebraic Geometry'' in 1991. He founded the journal ''Communications in Information and Systems'' in 2000, and has served as Editor-in-Chief since its inception.<ref name=":1" />

==Awards==
Yau was awarded the [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] in 1980 and the [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 2000. He was elected an [[IEEE Fellow]] in 2003 and a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2013.<ref name=":1" />
